feedback: Evidence: iterations 0 to 5 all ended off_track with max_error of about 0.061 m on every track. Span ±0.05 m removed line loss on oval and slalom (iteration 1). The 16 mm footprint kept line loss at zero but did not move max_error (iteration 2). Sensor y 0.06 with ki 0.3 brought line loss back on the s-bend and slalom and left max_error at 0.061 m (iteration 3). wheel_track 0.15 m with kp 4.4 kept max_error the same and raised control effort (iteration 4). Mass 0.6 kg (iteration 5) scored 26.9876, below iteration 2's 26.9949, with no clear max_error gain. So far, nothing except span has changed line loss, and nothing has moved max_error. Your y = 0.02 test is the right next step: it shortens look-ahead without the ki confound from iteration 3, and the controller keeps the iteration-2 gains. The outcome of this race is not known yet. Read the result as follows. If the excursion is at the start of the run and y = 0.02 leaves max_error unchanged, the excursion is a start-up effect, and no sensor or wheel change is likely to remove it alone. If line loss returns at y = 0.02, the shorter look-ahead is not usable, so revert to y = 0.04.
requested_changes: Keep 16 mm footprints at x = ±0.05 m, mass 0.8 kg and wheel_track 0.12 m, and test y = 0.02 m as the single change. Report max_error and line_loss_events per track, and whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run.
If line_loss_events stay at zero and max_error falls below about 0.058 m, try y = 0.00 m as the next single change, since the shorter look-ahead is what helped.
If line loss returns at y = 0.02 m, revert to y = 0.04 m and keep the iteration-2 row, since y = 0.06 m already reintroduced line loss.
